Maya Chen: Quick bring-up notes for Hummingbird-9.2b — ran FP16/int6/int4 on 8xA100 testbed with a 10k mixed-query corpus (short chat, NLU, longform summarization). TL;DR: int6 looks like the sweet spot for unit econ vs quality; int4 gives bigger cost wins but regresses on longform and code. Thoughts? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Ian Park: Raw numbers paste below from the smoke runs:
```
Throughput (tokens/s): FP16 420, int6 600, int4 720
p50 latency (ms): FP16 18, int6 12.6, int4 10.5
p95 latency (ms): FP16 45, int6 30, int4 90 (cold KV warmup cases)
Unit cost per 1M toks: FP16 $28.9, int6 $11.9, int4 $7.6
Quality delta (GTN eval, higher is better): FP16 0.0, int6 -0.6, int4 -2.9
```

Devon Li: Confirmed: int4 drop concentrated on longform summarization (>=250 tokens) and multi-step code synthesis. Single-turn chat and short QA mostly fine.

Samir Patel: Can you slice those deltas by product-relevant buckets? Product/GTN care about NLU vs summarization separately.

Ian Park: Slice breakdown (10k sample, mixed weights):
- NLU (short Q/A): int4 -0.2, int6 -0.05
- Summarization (>=250 tokens): int4 -4.1, int6 -0.8
- Code/stepwise reasoning: int4 -3.7, int6 -0.9
- Conversational chit-chat: int4 -0.1, int6 -0.02

Leah Ortiz: From a product handoff POV: recommend enabling int6 as the default served weight for this model in hosted + dedicated. Gate int4 for budget paths but add quality guards for summarization and code.

Maya Chen: Proposed routing policy (draft):
- If expected output tokens <= 80 AND eval-proxy score >= 0.92 -> route to int4
- Else if expected output tokens <= 500 -> route to int6
- Else -> FP16 fallback for heavy longform tasks
Also: run daily evals on the summarization slice and trigger an alert if int4 drift > 2.0 pts.

EvalBot: New eval run scheduled: hummingbird-9.2b-int4-vs-int6-2026-03-23 triggered by @Maya Chen

Samir Patel: Product question: what's the back-of-envelope unit savings at scale? Example: 1B tokens/day.

Ian Park: Back-of-envelope math: per 1M tokens costs from smoke run -> FP16 $28.9, int6 $11.9, int4 $7.6.
- 1B tokens/day = 1000 * per-1M.
- FP16 = $28,900/day, int6 = $11,900/day, int4 = $7,600/day.
- Savings FP16->int6 ~= $17,000/day; FP16->int4 ~= $21,300/day.
(These are raw infra unit numbers; don't include caching, batching optimizations, or network egress.)

Devon Li: Ops note: int4 requires cached KV warmups; observed cold-start p99 penalty ~+60ms for the first requests on a warm shard. Need to ensure prefix caching and/or adaptive warmers in Dedicated.

Leah Ortiz: Ops/actionable: we need rollback flags, canary for routing policy, and a product-facing one-liner for docs. I'll open infra ticket and a route-config PR.

Maya Chen: I'll draft a concise scorecard snapshot for GTN: one table with slices (NLU, Summarize, Code, Chat), unit costs, quality deltas, and recommended routing rules. Plan to post by EOD.

DeployBot: deploy:route-update hummingbird-9.2b-int6-default canary started by @Leah Ortiz

Samir Patel: :thumbsup: Couple asks for the GTN handoff pack: 1) expected QoQ risk (short bullet), 2) suggested traffic splits for first 2 weeks, 3) rollback triggers (percent regression or user-visible metric).

Maya Chen: Will include those. Preliminary suggestion for initial split: 80% int6 default, 10% int4 gated to low-risk slices, 10% FP16 reserved for heavy longform customers. Rollback triggers: any slice-level regression >1.5 pts or p95 latency regress >20% vs baseline.

Ian Park: One more datapoint: enabling continuous prefix caching brings int4 p95 down to ~35ms (from 90ms in cold cases) and reduces longform delta by ~0.7 pts because fewer context-induced underflows. So caching + int4 gating looks promising.

Devon Li: If we expose the gating flags in Redwood Console we can let product flip the int4 budget per-customer quickly. Recommend a per-tenant int4 percentage knob + summarization holdout switch.

Leah Ortiz: I'll coordinate with devex to add the knobs to the route config UI and draft the short doc blurb for GTN.

Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll attach the scorecard snapshot and a short PR with suggested route config (canary + rollback rules) in this thread when ready.

Leah Ortiz: Thanks — scheduling infra sync for tomorrow to align canary windows.

Samir Patel: Great. If the snapshot quantifies the user-visible regressions clearly, we can start a soft rollout next week. :rocket:

Maya Chen: Attaching snapshot in thread shortly.
